The formula for the derivative of $arccsc$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}-2arccscx) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-2(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}+\frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of $\text{arccsc}$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\text{arccsc}\,x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2arccsc(8-{x}^{4})) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccsc(8-{x}^{4})) \\  & =2(-\frac{1}{|8-{x}^{4}|\sqrt{(8-{x}^{4})^{2}-1}})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8-{x}^{4}) \\  & =2(-\frac{1}{|8-{x}^{4}|\sqrt{(8-{x}^{4})^{2}-1}})\cdot (-4{x}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{8{x}^{3}}{|8-{x}^{4}|\sqrt{(8-{x}^{4})^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Product Rule
question.worked_solution:
The formulae for the derivatives of $arccsc$ and $arcsec$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx) & =-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =arcsecx\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)+arccscx\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) \\  & =arcsecx\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})+arccscx\cdot (\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}) \\  & =-\frac{arcsecx}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}+\frac{arccscx}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{arccscx-arcsecx}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Product Rule
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccot$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccotx)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(({x}^{3}+2x)arccotx) \\  & =arccotx\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+2x)+({x}^{3}+2x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccotx) \\  & =arccotx\cdot (3{x}^{2}+2)+({x}^{3}+2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}) \\  & =(3{x}^{2}+2)arccotx-\frac{{x}^{3}+2x}{{x}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Quotient Rule
question.worked_solution:
Here, we let $u(x)=arccscx$ and $v(x)={e}^{3x}-1$, and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=3{e}^{3x}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\cdot ({e}^{3x}-1)-arccscx\cdot 3{e}^{3x}}{({e}^{3x}-1)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{({e}^{3x}-1)|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}-\frac{3{e}^{3x}arccscx}{({e}^{3x}-1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions Using the Quotient Rule
question.worked_solution:
Here, we let $u(x)={x}^{2}+4x$ and $v(x)=arccscx,$ and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=2x+4\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(2x+4)\cdot arccscx-({x}^{2}+4x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})}{{arccsc}^{2}x} \\  & =\frac{2x+4}{arccscx}+\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\cdot {arccsc}^{2}x}.\end{aligned}
$$
